one_liner: MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a broad REST API with free self-serve API keys (digest) and service accounts (OAuth client-credentials); user-delegated OAuth is invite-only; official MCP exists.
auth_notes: Admin API accepts HTTP Digest with org/project API keys (legacy, classed as BASIC-style key pair) and service accounts via OAuth2 client-credentials. The authorization-code OAuth (App Connections) is invite-only with manually provisioned credentials, so OAUTH2 is not primary for multi-user.
access_notes: Free Atlas account; Organization Owner can create API keys or service accounts. Free M0 cluster available. Admin API does not expose cluster data.
blocker_notes: Self-serve credentials are available today. Multi-user delegated OAuth is invite-only, but per-customer API keys or service accounts work, and that does not count as friction.

evidence.quote: The API accepts 2 different authentication methods: Digest auth (http) Service accounts (oauth2)
MongoDB Atlas OAuth is currently **invite-only**. Client credentials are **not self-provisioned** — MongoDB provisions them manually on your behalf.
To create a service account or API keys for an organization, you must have Organization Owner access to that organization.
Free cluster (`M0`) | No cost | Learning MongoDB, prototyping, and other workloads that fit within the Atlas Free Cluster Limits.
To use the Atlas Administration API to manage your Atlas clusters, you must authenticate your API requests.
A Model Context Protocol server for interacting with MongoDB Databases and MongoDB Atlas.
MongoDB Atlas Managed MCP Server, which MongoDB hosts and manages for you in Atlas.
